result:
Round 476 is implemented but stopped for one ruling from B. The code reviewer raised a Medium on a file the task says must stay byte-identical to the sketch, and the D-29z1683 rule makes that a STOP. I left the tree exactly at the sketch state, so if B accepts it, C can run C1–C12 with no further pass from me.

**The STOP (R1, `SpotlightLoader.tsx:181`):** the loader overlay still sets its background with an inline style (`var(--color-background)`). It also has a child layer that paints the same colour with `bg-background`. The project's Tailwind-first rule would put `bg-background` on the overlay and drop both. Points for B's ruling:
- HEAD already had an inline style on that line (`'#000'`), so it isn't new.
- The product-designer ruling explicitly names "the overlay's inline style".
- The reviewer says it renders the same and isn't urgent.
- Editing it would break the sha check, the claims diff and three of the mutant pins.

**What was done:**
- K1 (HEAD `edeba5a`, clean tree) and K2 (sketch sha `83341e9f…`) matched before I started.
- The sketch applied with rc 0, and all 5 file sha256 values check OK.
- Doc 309 is written: the template headings in order, l.4 exact, and every test row id it names is real.
- After the code review I made three fixes, all in the doc (my own file):
  - the contrast figures had the two viewports swapped;
  - it called the old wordmark "white" when it was ivory;
  - it cited test rows E8 and L6, which don't exist; they are now E8b and E14.
- Only the 6 granted paths changed; no protected file was touched.

**Checks I ran (logs in `a-round-476/`):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck | rc 0 |
| lint | rc 0; 191 warnings and 1 info, the same counts as B's run |
| Biome on the 5 code files | rc 0; 2 existing warnings, both in `EntranceCover.tsx`, whose logic is unchanged |
| build | rc 0 |
| The 16 covering test files | all 262 tests pass; the entrance-loader file takes 941 ms, under half its timeout |
| B's claims script | byte-equal to the allowed output, ends `L58 OK` |
| Mutants | 12 of 12 fail the tests, with the same failing rows as B's run |

**Code review:** the project's `code-reviewer` agent ran and scored it 8/10, with no Critical or High findings. It had no shell, so it reviewed the working tree rather than the diff.
- **Lows, all in files that must stay byte-identical,** so they are reported and not edited (candidates for `deferred_low_polish`):
  - R2: a Georgian comment in `EntranceCover.tsx` still calls the first frame black.
  - R3: older English JSX comments remain in `SpotlightLoader.tsx`; they predate this round.
  - R4: test P3 only scans the source text, so it misses some black/white forms.
  - R5: test P2 hard-codes the particle count of 15.
  - R6: N3c's title mentions the footer, but the test only checks the header.
- **Architecture note:** keep the new dust-particle state inside `SpotlightLoader`; value and risk are both low, so no task is needed.

**Process gaps:**
- I read the pre-flight and `/check` skills only after applying the sketch, so the pre-flight gate was not published before the code went in.
- Four of the six primitives were read only in part.

**Not verified by me:** I ran no browser probe, so the browser rows C5–C10 and C12 (colours, wordmark contrast, timing, the product-page journey and auth) are C's work. The contrast figures in the doc are B's measurements; I did not re-measure them. I'm not marking DPG-P0-3a or the backlog complete.

The full report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-476.md`.
